definitions.explanation: The removal or elimination of people from an organization, especially for political reasons.
Eliminating undesirable elements or corruption from an organization or system.

examples.japanese: {独裁者|どくさいしゃ}は{反対派|はんたいは}を{粛清|しゅくせい}した。
{党内|とうない}で{大規模|だいきぼ}な{粛清|しゅくせい}が{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: A large-scale purge was carried out within the party.

examples.japanese: スターリン{時代|じだい}の{粛清|しゅくせい}で{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{犠牲|ぎせい}になった。
examples.english: Many people fell victim to the purges during the Stalin era.

examples.japanese: {組織|そしき}の{腐敗|ふはい}を{粛清|しゅくせい}する。
examples.english: To clean up the corruption in the organization.

examples.japanese: {社内|しゃない}の{不正|ふせい}を{粛清|しゅくせい}するための{調査|ちょうさ}が{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: An investigation to eliminate fraud within the company has begun.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{粛清|しゅくせい}の{対象|たいしょう}となり、{失脚|しっきゃく}した。
examples.english: He became a target of the purge and fell from power.

notes:
USAGE:
Often used in political and historical contexts, particularly regarding authoritarian regimes. Can also be used more broadly for cleaning up corruption.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {粛清|しゅくせい}の{嵐|あらし} - purge storm (wave of purges)
- {政治的|せいじてき}{粛清|しゅくせい} - political purge
- {大粛清|だいしゅくせい} - Great Purge (historical)
- {粛清|しゅくせい}{対象|たいしょう} - target of a purge

ETYMOLOGY:
The term is frequently associated with the Stalinist purges ({大粛清|だいしゅくせい}) and similar political cleansings in other countries.
